To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) it is technically possible to design a privacy-preserving monitoring system, where the monitoring application can perform its task while protecting the privacy of the monitored customers; (ii) the design of the privacy protection mechanism is highly application dependent, as different applications require different levels of privacy protection and different types of information from the monitored traffic traces; and (iii) there are several technical issues that must be resolved before the design of such systems can be considered as a viable solution.
(i) privacy-preserving monitoring can be technically feasible, (ii) privacy-preserving network traffic monitoring is not a trivial task and (iii) the research challenges are still significant.

(i) the use of encryption is a viable approach to protect privacy in network monitoring, (ii) the use of a two-tier system, where data protection and monitoring applications are separated, is feasible, (iii) the use of an intermediate layer between the two tiers, to facilitate communication, is feasible and (iv) the use of cryptographic techniques to provide data integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation is feasible.

the following issues: (1) how to design a network monitoring architecture that can be used to collect privacy-preserving traffic traces; (2) how to design suitable privacy protection mechanisms for traffic traces; and (3) how to design privacy-preserving monitoring applications.
